answer: Mirrored-work audit trail. Each identity must append a small signed pulse of settlement history to a shared log; a random week of any identity's past is recomputed by peers from countersigned receipts, and mismatches slash its reachable counterparties. Cloning is cheap only until every copy needs an independent, receipts-backed ember of genuine activity. Isolation is the leverage: an island of fresh clones cannot borrow history, and fabricating one costs a full audit trail per clone plus the slash.
